findings.summary: The counterexample test and the planned research section/takeaway under-represent the Department's own stated expectation about participant costs. 91 FR 69159-69160 and the regulatory analysis also say disclosure could lead to lower plan costs shared through premiums and lower participant out-of-pocket costs, say the final rule 'could have a bigger impact than CBO's estimates' because large self-insured plans are not subject to state disclosure laws, and cite Scanlon (2024): inter-firm disclosures raised plan costs 3.5 percent but reduced participant out-of-pocket costs 1 percent. sources.md fact 11 and the counterexample note cite only the CBO S. 1339 estimate and the 2025 Part D state-law study, so 'the Department's cited research calls the direct effect uncertain' is accurate but selective.
findings.fix: WRITE: add these Department statements and the Scanlon result to the evidence packet's closed fact list from the saved FR text (fr-2026-22306-text.txt, regulatory-impact sections 8.1, 8.3, 10-11), attributed to the Department and the cited researchers, and have Section 6 and the Takeaway state both directions (possible lower plan and out-of-pocket costs, uncertain pass-through to participants because rebates go to the plan and pass-through depends on plan design). Keep the verdict unchanged: the rule itself sets no copay and reaches no 2026 open-enrollment plan. AUDIT: check Section 6, the Takeaway and the FAQ for one-sided framing under the HIGH contrary-evidence check.

findings.summary: The brief says 'self-insured only'. The preamble summary says the rule applies only to self-insured plans of specified large employers and self-insured specified large plans, but the regulatory text in paragraph (b) defines covered plans by exclusion: it excludes a group health plan whose benefits are ALL provided exclusively through a health insurance policy, and plans of sponsors affiliated with a drug manufacturer, distributor, wholesaler, PBM or rebate aggregator. 'Specified large plan' (paragraph (m)(7)) refers to non-single-employer sponsors (29 U.S.C. 1002(16)(B)(ii)-(iii)), not to every plan with 100 participants.
findings.fix: WRITE: phrase coverage as 'large self-insured plans' with the regulatory-text exclusion stated beside the table (plans whose benefits are entirely insured are excluded), and describe 'specified large plan' accurately instead of implying any plan with 100 or more participants. Do not say 'self-insured only' without the paragraph (b) qualifier.

requestCoverage.evidence: Section 3 and Section 4 of the brief plan to state the disclosure content, recipients (responsible plan fiduciaries of large self-insured plans), cadence (before contracts, 90 days for renewals, semiannual, quarterly on request), effective date January 4, 2027 and applicability to plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2027, each attributed to 91 FR 69092 at first use. I verified every one of these against the saved Federal Register text and the live Federal Register API record; the plan does not narrow the request.

Section 1 places the verdict first (no change to plans chosen in 2026 open enrollment; plan type, plan-year and no-copay conditions), the planned Takeaway repeats it with the same conditions and the next action, and the FAQ is drawn from the rule text. The change/does-not-change split is supported by the regulatory text (no cost-sharing, premium or formulary requirement; disclosures to fiduciaries only). Binding finding CR-A1 requires the research section and takeaway to present the Department's own contrary-direction statements as well, without changing the verdict.
